subject: Addition of edge-caching partner — request for dataflow map & evidence
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@edgeanalytics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: New edge-caching partner — need subprocessor roster & dataflow map

Hi Alex / Marissa,

Quick heads up — Edge Analytics is starting a small pilot that will route a subset of inference traffic through a regional CDN/edge cache vendor (CacheGrid) for latency-sensitive customers. Procurement asked that we collect the following before we proceed with contract signature:

- Full subprocessor roster for any processors involved in handling or caching request payloads
- Short dataflow diagram showing where customer request/response bodies traverse (origin, edge, logs, analytics)
- Encryption (in transit and at rest) and retention guarantees for cached items
- Any planned cross-border transfers (EU/US) or third-country storage

We need this to complete our vendor security questionnaire and to feed into procurement's DPA amendment. Can you send the materials or point me at the right contact? Timeline: procurement would like evidence by EOD Friday, 05/07 if possible.

Thanks,
Liam
---
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Ops, Edge Analytics, Inc.
liam@edgeanalytics.com
+1 415-555-0102

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@edgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New edge-caching partner — need subprocessor roster & dataflow map

Liam — thanks for the note and the timeline. We're already evaluating CacheGrid for a limited read-cache layer (no user-PII storage by design), but happy to provide the artifacts you outlined.

Preliminary replies:
- We'll attach our current subprocessor inventory export for the services involved and call out CacheGrid as the proposed addition.
- I'll attach a short dataflow PNG that highlights where tokens and metadata may touch CacheGrid nodes. Important: for this pilot we're planning to only cache non-sensitive response fragments and not persist full request payloads.
- CacheGrid has TLS in transit; we're asking for ATR (at-rest) encryption details and a retention window; we'll share once they confirm.
- No planned cross-border storage beyond their regional nodes for this pilot (we'll include list of regions).

Attachments: subprocessor-inventory-20270504.csv, edge-cdn-dataflow-diagram.png (draft). I will follow up tomorrow after getting CacheGrid's ATR/retention confirmation and a DPA amendment draft.

If procurement needs anything specific in the DPA (e.g., logging controls, access reviews), loop that to me and I'll coordinate with Legal.

Best,
Alex

---
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: CacheGrid onboarding — legal questions & quick asks

Marissa / Karthik — following up on Liam's request. Draft notes for Legal/procurement review:

1) Data handling scope: pilot will allow caching of non-sensitive response snippets only. Need formal attest from CacheGrid that they will not persist full request payloads, or if they do, that it's encrypted with customer-controlled keys (KMS/HSM).
2) Logs & analytics: confirm that logs forwarded to their observability partner are redacted and that log retention complies with our 90-day default for pilot customers.
3) DPA amendment: we should require explicit subprocessor notification plus 30-day review window before CacheGrid goes live for production. For the pilot we can accept a shorter window but need Procurement sign-off.
4) Regions: confirm we get a list of CacheGrid's POPs and whether any are in APAC/EU for customers with residency constraints.

Can you: (a) have Legal review the dpa-amendment-draft.docx attached and add the clause around key control/KMS requirement, and (b) ask Infra to validate that the diagram (edge-cdn-dataflow-diagram.png) accurately reflects our planned prefix caching and that no KV caches will be persisted to the edge.

I'll coordinate with Liam and ask CacheGrid these direct questions. If Legal wants to meet the vendor, we should set up a 30-min call this week.

Thanks,
Alex

---
Note: attachment included for internal review: dpa-amendment-draft.docx

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@edgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@edgeanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New edge-caching partner — need subprocessor roster & dataflow map

Hi Liam — quick update following Legal & Procurement review. Thanks for your patience.

Summary / next steps:
- We've attached the formal subprocessor inventory export and a revised dataflow diagram that includes explicit notes on what is cached vs transient. (attachments: subprocessor-inventory-20270504.csv; edge-cdn-dataflow-diagram.png)
- CacheGrid confirmed: TLS v1.2+ in transit; ATR encryption supported via provider-managed keys. They have offered customer-managed encryption (bring-your-own-key) as an enterprise option — Legal flagged that as preferable for customers with strict residency/KMS requirements.
- Retention: CacheGrid's default cache TTL is 48 hours; they offered a configurable TTL down to 1 hour and a maximum retention of 7 days for audit logs.
- Cross-border: CacheGrid POPs for the pilot are US-East, US-West, EU-West. No APAC POPs in the pilot.
- DPA amendment: attached is a DocuSign-ready DPA amendment draft (link below). Procurement asked for a 7-day pilot notification window, Legal recommends 30 days for production. For the pilot only, we can proceed with a signed amendment and a 7-day review window.

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning?token=abc123-edge-dpa
Drive (review copy): https://docs.google.com/d/1aBcDEF_shared_dpa_draft

If that works, please sign the amendment and confirm the pilot start range (we're proposing target window 2027-05-15 -> 2027-05-22). If Procurement needs any further evidence, let me know and I'll escalate to Legal immediately.

Best,
Alex

---
Attachments referenced above are included as stubs: subprocessor-inventory-20270504.csv, edge-cdn-dataflow-diagram.png, dpa-amendment-draft.docx
